inputs.net_debt_basis: Net cash including marketable securities: total_debt (119,074, per Q1-2026 10-Q balance sheet long-term debt) - (cash 101,816 + marketable securities 41,273) = -24,015 (net CASH position). Amazon's Q1-2026 10-Q reports combined cash+equivalents+marketable securities of $143.1B, which is the more accurate liquid-asset base for a company that actively invests excess cash in short/intermediate marketable debt securities rather than holding it all as cash. A cash-only net debt (excluding the $41.3B of marketable securities) would be +17,258 (net debt); using net cash (-24,015) is more representative of true balance sheet strength and is the basis used throughout this model.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 FCF of $11.2B is a capex-cycle trough (128.3B cash capex, up from 77.7B in FY2024) and is NOT used directly as the DCF FCF base -- see fcf_modeling_note below.

fcf_modeling_note: Amazon's FY2025 FCF ($11.2B, 1.6% margin) and FY2024 FCF ($38.2B, 6.0% margin) both understate normalized earning power and are unsuitable as a naive 'take last year and grow it' DCF base. FY2025 is a deliberate investment trough (guided ~$200B 2026 capex vs $131.8B FY2025 cash capex) for AWS/AI data centers, Trainium silicon, and power infrastructure. Rather than growing a single base-year FCF figure, this model projects revenue (10-11% base growth decelerating per the 5yr/3yr revenue CAGR of 13.2%/11.7%) and applies an FCF-margin path that starts depressed (2.5% base case Year 1, reflecting continued heavy 2026-27 capex) and normalizes toward 8.5% of revenue by Year 5 as the AI capex cycle matures and AWS operating leverage flows through. This is conservative relative to Amazon's operating cash flow margin trajectory (14.8% FY2023 -> 18.2% FY2024 -> 19.5% FY2025, still rising), which implies FCF margin could recover toward 8-10%+ once capex intensity falls back from the current 17.9% of revenue toward a more normal 11-13% post-buildout run rate. Historical (pre-AI-supercycle) FCF margins of 6.0-9.2% (FY2019-FY2024, excluding FY2021-22 pandemic-hangover troughs and the FY2025-26 AI buildout trough) anchor the plausible range for Year 5 normalization.

historical_growth.eps_cagr_note: EPS 3yr CAGR is undefined: FY2022 EPS was -$0.27 (negative base, driven by a large non-cash Rivian mark-to-market loss), making a CAGR calculation meaningless. EPS 5yr CAGR (FY2020 $2.09 -> FY2025 $7.17 = 28.0%) is inflated by (a) the low FY2020 base, (b) large non-cash equity-stake gains/losses (Rivian, Anthropic) that swing GAAP EPS well outside underlying operating earnings power, and (c) FY2022's negative print mechanically flattering the subsequent recovery. EPS growth is not used as a DCF driver for these reasons.
historical_growth.fcf_cagr_note: FCF CAGR is not meaningful: FCF was negative in FY2021 (-$9.1B) and FY2022 (-$11.6B, pandemic-era fulfillment overbuild) and troughed again in FY2025 ($11.2B, AI capex buildout). No clean positive start/end pair spans a representative period. FY2016-FY2025 raw FCF path: [10535, 8376, 19400, 25825, 31020, -9069, -11569, 36813, 38219, 11194] $M.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr (with 5yr cagr of 13.2% as corroborating upper bound)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (41.2% 3yr / 34.5% 5yr) diverges massively (>200%) from revenue CAGR (11.7%/13.2%). This is NOT treated as a red flag on revenue quality -- it reflects that Amazon retains 100% of net income (no dividends, minimal buybacks in this window) while GAAP net income has been inflated by large non-cash equity-stake gains (Rivian warrants, Anthropic investment mark-ups: +$15.2B in FY2025, +$16.8B in Q1 2026 alone) that compound book value far faster than the underlying operating business. Per standard practice, equity CAGR is REJECTED as the growth driver here and revenue CAGR is used instead, consistent with the task-level guidance for this ticker.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Amazon is mid-way through an unprecedented, multi-year AI/cloud infrastructure buildout (~$200B guided 2026 capex, up from $131.8B in FY2025 and $77.7B in FY2024) directed at AWS data centers, power, and custom Trainium silicon to serve surging generative-AI compute demand (Anthropic, OpenAI multi-year commitments in the $100B+ range each). This capex program has temporarily crushed free cash flow (from $38.2B FY2024 to $11.2B FY2025) even as operating cash flow margin continues to climb (14.8% -> 18.2% -> 19.5% over FY2023-FY2025) and AWS growth has reaccelerated to 28% YoY (Q1 2026, fastest in 15 quarters). Rather than anchoring on either the depressed FY2025 FCF or the prior FY2024 'peak,' the model projects revenue growth (decelerating from the ~11-15% historical CAGR range toward terminal growth) and an FCF-margin path that stays depressed through the heavy-capex years (Y1-Y2) before normalizing toward historically-precedented margins (6-12%, depending on scenario) by Year 5 as the AI capex cycle matures and revenue from AI workloads (AWS AI run-rate already exceeding $15B) scales against a moderating capital base.

fcf_margin_path.rationale: Base Y5 margin of 8.5% sits within the pre-AI-supercycle historical range (FY2019 9.2%, FY2020 8.0%, FY2023 6.4%, FY2024 6.0%) and is conservative relative to the rising OCF margin trend (19.5% and climbing) net of a capex intensity that management/analysts broadly expect to normalize from FY2025's 17.9%-of-revenue peak back toward an 11-13% steady state post-buildout (FY2023 was 8.4%). Bull case assumes AI monetization (AWS AI run-rate, advertising) drives margin above the pre-AI-supercycle historical range as operating leverage compounds. Bear case assumes capex intensity stays structurally elevated (AI overbuild / slower depreciation runoff) and retail margin pressure (tariffs, competition) persists, capping FCF margin well below history.

wacc_rationale.note: Mega-cap, investment-grade balance sheet, low historical beta support a WACC toward the low end of the typical 8-11% large-cap range. A modest premium above the very largest mega-caps (e.g., AAPL/MSFT ~8-8.5%) is applied given elevated near-term execution risk on the ~$200B AI capex program (equipment obsolescence risk, AI-demand-mismatch risk, and ~$53B of new debt issued in Q1 2026 to help fund the buildout, raising interest-rate sensitivity). Bull case assumes execution de-risks (AI capacity monetizes on schedule); bear case assumes capex overbuild proves value-destructive, raising the discount rate applied to more uncertain, further-out cash flows.

base.growth_narrative: Revenue growth decelerates from ~10.5% (Y1, roughly in line with Q2-2026 guidance of 11-14% and consensus deceleration) toward 8.5% by Y5, consistent with the 3yr/5yr revenue CAGR of 11.7%/13.2% moderating as the business matures. FCF margin stays depressed through Y1-Y2 (2.5%/4.5%) reflecting continued ~$200B+ capex intensity, then recovers toward 6.0%/7.5%/8.5% in Y3-Y5 as AWS/AI capacity monetizes and capex intensity normalizes from the FY2025-26 buildout peak.

bull.growth_narrative: AWS/AI reacceleration sustains (28% Q1-2026 AWS growth persists/extends on Anthropic/OpenAI multi-year compute commitments and Trainium3 price-performance advantage); advertising continues compounding at a high-margin, low-capex rate; retail margin structurally improves (record 13.1% Q1-2026 consolidated operating margin extends). FCF margin recovers faster and to a higher terminal level (12% by Y5) as AI capacity utilization and depreciation runoff both work in Amazon's favor ahead of schedule.

bear.growth_narrative: AI infrastructure overbuild risk materializes: AWS demand growth decelerates as AI compute capacity outpaces monetizable workloads, equipment depreciation/obsolescence accelerates, and a portion of the ~$200B+ capex program proves to generate sub-hurdle returns. Simultaneously, tariff-driven cost inflation and intensifying competition (Temu/Shein, Walmart) compress thin retail margins further. FCF margin stays structurally suppressed (5% by Y5, below even the pre-AI-supercycle historical range) as elevated capex intensity persists longer than the base case assumes.

valuation.note: Net debt = -24,015 (net CASH position including marketable securities), so equity value = enterprise value + 24,015.

current_ev_fcf_comparison.note: Current EV/FCF is 220.8x on trough FY2025 FCF ($11.2B) -- a meaningless multiple given the denominator is artificially depressed by the capex supercycle, not a genuine earnings signal. Using FY2024 pre-supercycle FCF ($38.2B) as a rough proxy, current EV/FCF is ~64.7x. All three scenarios' implied exit multiples (11.7x-18.8x, applied to a much larger, margin-normalized Year-5 FCF base) sit well BELOW this pre-supercycle proxy multiple, meaning the model does NOT assume multiple expansion versus history -- it assumes FCF normalizes toward a level the market is already effectively pricing via its willingness to hold AMZN through the trough.

entry_price.note: Entry Price = ( sum(FCF_t / 1.15^t, t=1..5) + Gordon_TV_5 / 1.15^5 - net_debt ) / shares. TV_5 computed at WACC (fair year-5 exit value); only discounting back to today uses the 15% hurdle. net_debt = -24,015 (net cash), so equity value = discounted flows + 24,015.

base.interpretation: Base-case entry price ($86.18) is 62.9% below the current price of $232.11. At current prices, a buyer holding through Year 5 and exiting at the base-case Gordon terminal value would earn well below a 15% IRR -- consistent with the base intrinsic value ($107.97) also sitting far below the current price.

bull.interpretation: Bull-case entry price ($169.94) is 26.8% below current price. Even if the bull scenario (sustained AWS/AI reacceleration, faster margin normalization) materializes, today's price does not yet offer a 15% IRR entry point -- though the gap is much narrower than in the base/bear cases.

bear.interpretation: Bear-case entry price ($35.60) is 84.7% below current price, reflecting that a bear scenario (AI capex overbuild, margin compression) would require a dramatically lower entry point to clear a 15% hurdle.

sensitivity.basis: Base-case FCF path (revenue growth 10.5/10.0/9.5/9.0/8.5%, FCF margin 2.5/4.5/6.0/7.5/8.5% of revenue). Net debt = -24,015 (net cash). Values in USD per share.

probability_weighted.weight_rationale: Standard 50/25/25 base/bull/bear weighting. Even the probability-weighted IV ($119.73) sits well below the current price ($232.11), implying the market is pricing a scenario more optimistic than this model's bull case (IV $220.94, essentially in line with current price) -- i.e., the market appears to be underwriting sustained AWS/AI reacceleration AND faster-than-historical FCF margin normalization simultaneously. This should be read as a signal that AMZN's current valuation depends heavily on the AI capex program paying off faster and at a higher terminal margin than this model's bull case assumes, not as a mechanical 'sell' signal -- see caveats below.

model_caveats: This is a mechanical revenue x FCF-margin DCF; it does not explicitly model the AWS/Advertising/Retail segment mix shift that is the actual driver of Amazon's margin structure. A sum-of-the-parts approach (separately valuing AWS at a cloud-infra multiple, advertising at an ad-business multiple, and retail at a thin-margin multiple) would likely produce a materially higher valuation, since AWS alone (28% growth, ~35% operating margin) is worth a premium multiple on a standalone basis that a single consolidated FCF-margin path understates.

All three scenarios show negative upside vs. the current $232.11 price, including the bull case (-4.8%). This does not necessarily mean AMZN is overvalued -- it means a consolidated-FCF DCF using historically-grounded margin assumptions is a conservative lens for a company mid-cycle in transforming its margin structure via AWS/AI/advertising mix shift. Investors should weight this DCF alongside segment-level (SOTP) and multiples-based cross-checks.

The ~$200B FY2026 capex guide is unprecedented in scale; if AI compute demand growth disappoints or Trainium economics underperform, the base/bear cases could still prove optimistic on how quickly FCF margin normalizes.

Net debt is modeled as net CASH of -$24,015M (including $41.3B of marketable securities). If capex continues to be debt-funded at the pace seen in Q1 2026 (~$53B raised), this net-cash cushion could erode over the projection period; this model treats net debt as a static Day-0 balance sheet item per the standard DCF methodology.

historical_averages.note: FY-end Dec closes, split-adjusted; FY2022 excluded from P/E (negative EPS)

sanity_check.diagnosis: No over-valuation trip. Base-case IV $107.97 implies 15.1x P/E and 2.8x P/B on FY2025 actuals — far BELOW the 10yr averages (83.5x P/E, 12.8x P/B) and below even the 10yr minimums (32.2x, 5.9x). The consolidated revenue-times-FCF-margin DCF is conservative relative to any multiple the market has paid for AMZN in a decade; the gap reflects the sum-of-the-parts limitation documented in model_caveats (AWS at ~35% margin growing 28% would command a premium multiple standalone).
